primary_task: Audit a design or page (Figma URL, URL or description) against WCAG 2.1 AA and output a structured findings report with priority fixes.

requirements.name: the design or page to audit (Figma URL, URL, or description)
requirements.evidence: "Audit for accessibility: @$1"; argument-hint "<Figma URL, URL, or description>" (alternatives; any one suffices)
requirements.basis: web_fetch: fetch a web page or unauthenticated API by URL; and user_conversation grant for a description

requirements.name: ~~design tool (Figma)
requirements.evidence: "If ~~design tool is connected: Inspect color values ... directly from Figma"
requirements.basis: lacks: connectors or integrations other than the tools listed

requirements.name: ~~project tracker
requirements.evidence: "If ~~project tracker is connected: Create tickets for each accessibility finding"
requirements.basis: lacks: connectors or integrations other than the tools listed

requirements.name: screen readers (VoiceOver, NVDA)
requirements.evidence: Testing Approach: "3. Screen reader testing (VoiceOver, NVDA)"; Tips: "My audit is a great start, but manual testing with VoiceOver/NVDA catches things I can't."
requirements.basis: lacks: Windows or macOS, and their GUI toolchains (Xcode, Visual Studio, PowerShell on Windows)

requirements.name: automated accessibility scanner / browser for keyboard testing
requirements.basis: The manifest does not name a scanner or browser; one could be installed from npm but no browser is stated.

notes: The connectors are conditional ('If ... connected') and screen-reader testing is acknowledged as outside the audit. If a Figma URL were the only accepted input the verdict would be BLOCKED; the document accepts a description or URL instead.
